stem: A heart transplant candidate with a significant smoking history asks why continued smoking cessation counseling matters after listing. Which post-transplant risk should the coordinator emphasize?

options.text: Increased risk of coronary atherosclerosis, graft dysfunction, and graft loss
Smoking history has no measurable effect on heart graft outcomes
Smoking only affects kidney grafts, not cardiac allografts
Continued smoking is recommended to reduce immunosuppression side effects

explanation.rationale_correct: Heart transplant recipients with a smoking history have an increased risk of developing coronary atherosclerosis, graft dysfunction, and loss after transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Smoking history is associated with measurable adverse cardiac graft outcomes.
rationale_incorrect.C: Smoking adversely affects heart transplant recipients specifically, not only kidney recipients.
rationale_incorrect.D: Smoking increases cardiovascular and graft risks; it is not recommended to offset immunosuppression effects.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Heart transplant recipients with a smoking history have an increased risk of developing coronary atherosclerosis, graft dysfunction, and loss

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → J. Consultations → 2. Pulmonary evaluation → d. Effects of smoking in specific transplant populations → e.i. (heart graft risks); PDF p. 33 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 010200 item; first heart-organ smoking-risk angle; anchor verified on Cupples p. 33.

stem: During lung transplant evaluation education, what participation requirement should the coordinator explain for most candidates before listing?

options.text: A pulmonary rehabilitation program several times per week
No structured exercise because activity is permanently contraindicated
Immediate living donor identification before any other testing
Annual re-listing as a new candidate entry every 12 months

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates for lung transplantation are usually required to participate in a pulmonary rehabilitation program several times a week as part of evaluation and preparation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Pulmonary rehabilitation is typically required, not permanent activity restriction without structured rehab.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lung transplantation uses deceased donors; living donor identification is not the standard listing prerequisite described here.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist maintenance involves status updates, not mandatory annual re-registration as a new candidate.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: required to participate in a pulmonary rehabilitation program several times a week

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → Waitlist Management → 5. Lung transplant candidates → a. (pulmonary rehabilitation requirement); PDF p. 54 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 010400 item; lung evaluation-process angle distinct from LAS updates (cctc-2021); anchor verified on Cupples p. 54.

stem: A pediatric solid-organ recipient is approaching adolescence. Which inactivated vaccination should post-transplant health-maintenance teaching prioritize before sexual activity?

options.text: Live herpes zoster vaccine during high-dose steroid therapy
No vaccinations because all are permanently contraindicated after transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Post-transplant health maintenance includes human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination for pediatric patients prior to sexual activity, along with other inactivated vaccines per program protocol.

rationale_incorrect.B: Live varicella vaccine is contraindicated after transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Live herpes zoster vaccine is contraindicated after transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Inactivated vaccines such as HPV are recommended; live-virus vaccines are restricted, not all vaccinations.

stem: A liver transplant candidate who continues to smoke asks about transplant-specific risks beyond general cardiovascular disease. Which liver-related complication should education include?

options.text: Increased incidence of hepatic artery thrombosis
Elimination of all cardiovascular mortality risk after transplant
No association between smoking and liver graft vascular complications

explanation.rationale_correct: Cigarette smoking in liver transplant recipients has been implicated in cardiovascular mortality and an increased incidence of hepatic artery thrombosis.

rationale_incorrect.B: Smoking increases cardiovascular mortality risk rather than eliminating it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Smoking does not protect against biliary or vascular complications.
rationale_incorrect.D: Smoking is specifically associated with hepatic artery thrombosis among liver recipients.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Cigarette smoking has been implicated … increased incidence of hepatic artery thrombosis
